transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-29 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~47m
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Omar Singh (Redwood SE), Jia Chen (Redwood SE), Aaron Cho (CTO, Skiplist), Maya Ortiz (ML Eng), Priya Nair (Product)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Overall KV/prefix cache hit-rate improved with recent heuristic prefetch, but tail variability remains.
- Actionable tuning: adjust time-decay eviction, tighten prefix normalization, add session-cohort prefetching for mobile flows.
- Next: 48h continuous prefetch run, data handoff of session traces, security docs.

Topics: hit-rate numbers, eviction strategy, prompt reuse taxonomy, staging perf run, security/compliance ask, next steps.

Transcript body:
00:00 Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have the usual suspects, just quick roll call?
00:07 Aaron: Aaron here, yes, thanks Lena.
00:09 Maya: Maya on the call.
00:11 Omar: Omar from Redwood, hi.
00:13 Priya: Priya, hi.
00:15 Jia: Jia joining, quick note: I'll take notes on the config changes.

03:22 Lena: quick agenda, we'll run through last week's benchmark, hit-rate charts, discuss why mobile cohort dipped, then talk about eviction tuning and next steps. If we run out of time we'll prioritize the staging run plan.

06:05 Omar: ok so quick snapshot — after rolling the prefetch heuristic last Tuesday to staging we saw median KV hit-rate for the web cohort move from about 12% to 38%. The mobile cohort went from 9% to 21% but with big variance across session lengths. We did a couple of small fixes: prefix normalization for punctuation and a light-weight fingerprinting to avoid duplicates.
06:40 Maya: when you say prefix normalization, is that stripping trailing punctuation or are you normalizing whitespace too? We saw some prompts that only differ by a trailing comma.
06:48 Omar: yes both — primarily punctuation and whitespace collapse. We also normalize certain stop-words in the prefix key, that helped a lot. Still, mobile flows tend to have more short, one-shot prompts so reuse is inherently lower.

09:12 Aaron: curious about latency — did the prefetch add any instability? Our SLAs are tight on 95th.
09:20 Omar: good q. End-to-end p95 for the prefetch-enabled staging run actually dropped from ~380ms to ~220ms for web because caching avoided repeated KV loads and allowed smaller batch windows. For mobile, p95 is noisier: improved on average but occasional spikes when prefetch batch overlapped a heavy request stream.
09:47 Priya: ok that aligns with what we saw in production traces — spikes align to login bursts and certain event-driven flows.

12:31 Jia: technical note — we instrumented a per-prefix TTL and a time-decay eviction; default was 24h, we tried 6h for the mobile cohort and that reduced false positives where outdated context was reused. But shorter TTL reduced hit-rate for long-running sessions. It's a tradeoff.
12:58 Maya: can you quantify the tradeoff? what hit-rate loss vs staleness reduction?
13:05 Omar: yeah, on a 7-day window, the 24h TTL had 42% hit-rate for web long sessions and 28% for mobile. With 6h TTL mobile hit-rate went down to 18% but incorrect reuse cases (semantic mismatch) dropped by 62% in our evaluation.

16:40 Aaron: semantic mismatch is the big one for us — inaccurate reuse creates visible UX defects. I'd rather lose some hit-rate if it prevents hallucinated or context-leak answers.
16:53 Lena: totally, and that's why we suggested combining TTL with a lightweight semantic signature — a small embedding-based fingerprint that filters reuse candidates. That prevents old-but-similar prefixes from being reused when meaning changed.
17:12 Maya: embeddings are heavier — do you run them at query-time? concern about cost.
17:20 Omar: precompute for long-running sessions where we already have embeddings; for short mobile requests we rely on cheaper heuristics. The plan is hybrid. We'll share the cost delta in the csv.

20:00 Priya: question on session affinity — is the caching keyed by session id or by user id? We have ephemeral sessions on mobile so session id churn is high.
20:12 Jia: by default it's session-id first, then fallback to user-id if present. For Skiplist we can flip to user-id for mobile cohort to increase reuse, but that carries privacy and cross-session leakage risks.
20:34 Aaron: data residency and privacy are big for us — can't unify sessions across devices for certain PII flows.
20:40 Lena: we documented a config toggle: per-cohort keying. So you can keep user-id keying off for mobile and enable for web. We'll add that to the staging run.

23:58 Omar: another point — prefetch budget. We saw prefetch increased egress tokens by ~6% during peak, but reduced overall compute tokens by ~18% due to fewer repeated forward passes. Net cost per 1M tokens dropped by about 7% in our model. Those are model- and workload-dependent numbers, of course.
24:32 Maya: can you share the token accounting? Is that the CSV you mentioned?
24:36 Omar: yep, sharing the CSV with breakdown: prefetch tokens, cache hits avoided, tokens saved at model inference. Link will be in next_steps.

27:10 Aaron: regarding security/compliance — our InfoSec asked for audit logs for prefix reuse and a way to purge cache entries for a given user on demand.
27:23 Lena: we support purge-by-key and audit logs for cache hits at the request-id granularity. We'll send the SOC2 and audit link. Note: purge is async but we can do a near-real-time-on-demand purge for sensitive flows.
27:48 Priya: how does purge interact with prefetch? if someone requests purge right after prefetch ran, risk of stale reads?
28:00 Omar: good catch — purge is prioritized, but if a prefetch is in-flight we mark the prefetch candidates invalid and drop them. There is a ~200-400ms race window; we can tighten that by forcing sync invalidation for high-risk keys.

31:05 Maya: about prompt taxonomy — we exported the top 150 prefixes that generate 80% of traffic. Many are system prompts and some are noisy user-generated short queries. We think normalizing system prompts separately will bump effective hit-rate.
31:21 Omar: absolutely. We recommend a prompt-class mapping: system, ui-template, user-query, instructions. Treat system and ui-template prefixes as high-value for prefetch and longer TTL.

33:58 Aaron: did you try coalescing near-duplicate prefixes rather than exact-match keys?
34:05 Omar: yes, we experimented with a fuzzy coalescer (n-gram overlap threshold) — it gained another 5-7% absolute hit-rate for web but introduced a few false positives; so it's opt-in. We're thinking of a conservative threshold and a manual whitelist.

36:40 Priya: regarding metrics we need in our dashboard — hit-rate by cohort + p95 latency + incorrect-reuse rate + cost delta. Also desire to see top offending prefixes.
36:52 Lena: we'll share a Grafana dashboard template and metrics mapping.

39:12 Jia: quick note on eviction — we implemented a small LRU shard per GPU and a global time-decay sweeper. The sweeper runs every 5m by default but we can make it per-cohort. That cut mem thrash for heavy customers.
39:31 Maya: do you expose the eviction policy config in the private deployment? we want to tune in prod-like env.
39:39 Omar: yes, in Dedicated/Private you get full config knobs: TTL, LRU shard count, decay factor, prefetch budget. Hosted we can change via feature flags for pilots.

42:00 Aaron: what's the proposed next milestone?
42:05 Lena: run a continuous 48h prefetch with per-cohort configs (mobile: 6h TTL + user-id off; web: 24h TTL + user-id on; fuzzing off by default). Collect traces and csv, then do a perf deep-dive next week.
42:22 Omar: also we'll push the time-decay eviction change to staging and record the before/after hit-rate in the shared spreadsheet.

45:01 Maya: one last ask — can you add a column for observed UX regressions in the trace export? we can tag sessions where customer support flagged problem.
45:12 Jia: yes we'll add a flag and example session ids.

46:30 Lena: recap of owners and dates, thanks all. We'll send meeting notes and links.
